summary:
Plan written for w96 (migration-tools r7, r18, r25, r26). One question is open.
The accepted scenarios pass today and must stay green. Each fix (N4, N5, N6, N8, F7, F8, F9, F12) gets a test in tests/scripts/.
Decisions taken: status and upgrade refuse a version that is not a version, exit 1 (r18, r7). N5 rewrites only name values; #r<n> tokens and comments are left (r26).
N4 names the field and removes repeated lines. F8 is refused through the plan's failures, only when a work-item needs the id (r7, r26). F9 breaks ties by initiative name (r25).
The symbolic-link version-file defect is out of scope.
No existing test breaks (checked by search; there is no coverage map).
Open: what `migrate status --hook` does with a version file that holds no version.
questions: F7: when `.shop/plugin-version` holds no version (e.g. `next`, or nothing), what does `migrate status --hook`, the SessionStart hook, do? `--hook`'s help says it exits 0; the work-item says 'refuse, saying why'; no requirement settles which governs. Reading A, exit 0 with text: the hook prints to stdout a line saying the version file holds no version, naming what it holds and telling the session to tell the person. The session is told at its start and passes it on, and the hook keeps its exit-0 contract. Reading B, exit 1 as `migrate status` does: the hook prints the reason on stderr and exits 1. The session's context gets nothing; the person sees only the hook error that Claude Code reports, and the session never learns why.
